scope: read-only non-UI Android emulator network diagnosis; the existing status.sh probe already used write/flush, 250ms delay, and EOF

network.initial_disruption: At the 21:20 observation, WiFi was unassociated and no route was present; cmd wifi reconnect plus svc data enable restored association and routing before the post-recovery probes.

probe.request: GET /api/v1/health HTTP/1.1 with Host and Connection: close
probe.interpretation: The immediate-EOF comparison was an adhoc probe run after connectivity recovery; it demonstrates a probe timing race for that temporary command only and does not explain the original status.sh result or imply that status.sh lacked the 250ms delay.

conclusion: The 21:20 WiFi association/route loss was real. After reconnect, Android-to-host routing/NAT and both host listeners were healthy. The adhoc immediate-EOF probe also had a separate timing false negative; it must not be used as the cause of the earlier no-route status.
recommended_probe: write request; flush; wait 250ms; close stdin; wait/read with bounded timeout; assert HTTP 200
status_script_change: Layered no-route/TCP/HTTP diagnostics plus bounded process-group cleanup on HTTP probe timeout; the original status probe already had the 250ms flush/EOF sequence.
